in any programming language, what is the: A "for" loop repeats a block of code once for each item or index in an array, which makes it the classic way to go through a list. Most languages also offer shortcuts like "for each" or "map".
according to the international system of: In the International System of Units (SI), "kilo" means 1,000, so a kilobyte is 1,000 bytes. The count of 1,024 bytes is properly called a kibibyte, though many people still say kilobyte for it.
which computer hardware device provides: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects the processor, memory, storage and other parts so they can talk to each other. Everything else plugs into it.
what is the code name for the mobile ope: Android 7.0, released in 2016, was code-named Nougat. Google names its versions' sweet treats in alphabetical order up to Android 9, after which it switched to plain numbers.
in networking, what does ospf stand for?: OSPF stands for Open Shortest Path First, a routing protocol that lets routers share information about their links and calculate the shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm. It is widely used inside large company networks.
what is largely considered the precursor: USB, introduced in 1996, was designed to replace the many separate ports on older PCs. The PS/2 port, which IBM introduced in 1987 for keyboards and mice, is the one most often named as its predecessor.
approximately how many apple i personal: About 200 Apple I computers were built by hand in 1976, mostly by Steve Wozniak, and roughly 175 were sold. It originally cost $666.66, and surviving units are now worth huge sums to collectors.
moore's law originally stated that the n: In 1965, Gordon Moore predicted that the number of transistors on a chip would double every year. In 1975 he revised it to every two years, and the idea became known as Moore's law.
what was the first commerically availabl: The Intel 4004, released in 1971, was the first commercially available microprocessor. This 4-bit chip was first designed for a Busicom calculator.
which coding language was the #1 program: JavaScript was the most-used language on GitHub in 2015. It runs in every web browser, which is a big reason for its popularity.
which of the following is a personal com: The Fujitsu FM-7 was a home computer sold in Japan starting in 1982. Japanese companies like Fujitsu, NEC and Sharp had their own computer lines in the 1980s that never became popular in the West.
which of the following languages is used: Unity games are scripted in C# (pronounced "C sharp"), Microsoft's object-oriented programming language. Earlier versions also supported a JavaScript-like language called UnityScript.
what did the name of the tor anonymity n: Tor originally stood for "The Onion Router". The name refers to wrapping your traffic in layers of encryption, like the layers of an onion, as it passes through several relays.
in the server hosting industry iaas stan: IaaS is Infrastructure as a Service, where a company rents servers, storage and networking from a provider instead of buying them. Amazon Web Services' EC2 is a well-known example.
generally, which component of a computer: The graphics card (GPU) usually draws the most power in a computer, especially during gaming or heavy rendering. Processors come second.
when did the online streaming service \": Mixer began in 2016 as a streaming service called Beam, and was renamed Mixer in 2017 after Microsoft bought it. It shut down in 2020.
in programming, the ternary operator is: The ternary operator uses ?: and works like a short if/else: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse. It is called "ternary" because it takes three operands.
which of these programming languages is: Assembly language is a low-level language that maps almost one-to-one onto a processor's machine instructions. High-level languages such as Python or Java are easier for people to read and write.
in the programming language \"python\",: In Python, print("Hello World") displays the text. In Python 2 it was a statement without parentheses, but in Python 3 it became a regular function.
in programming, what do you call functio: Overloading means defining several functions with the same name but different parameters, and the compiler picks the right one for each call. Overriding is different: it replaces a parent class's method in a subclass.
what was bitcoin's block size limit in 2: Bitcoin's block size limit was set to 1 MB in 2010, a cap that was added to prevent spam. It later became a hot debate about scaling.
on which day did the world wide web go o: The first web page went online at CERN on December 20, 1990, built by Tim Berners-Lee. The web opened to the general public in 1991.
the teapot often seen in many 3d modelin: The Utah teapot was modeled by Martin Newell at the University of Utah in 1975. It became a standard test object in 3D graphics because its curves are complex but easy to model.
which of these people was not a founder: Apple was founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne. Jony Ive, who later designed products such as the iMac and iPhone, joined the company in 1992.
what type of sound chip does the super n: The SNES sound system used a Sony-designed chip, the SPC700, together with a sampler that played back short compressed sounds. That is why SNES music sounds like real instruments, rather than the simple beeps of earlier consoles.
what is the codename of the eighth gener: Coffee Lake was the codename of Intel's eighth-generation Core processors, launched in October 2017. It was the first mainstream Intel desktop line to offer six cores.
what was the first company to use the te: "Golden Master" is the final version of software that is ready to be copied and sold. Apple used the term, which it still uses for its pre-release builds.
which of these was the name of a bug fou: Heartbleed, found in April 2014, was a serious flaw in OpenSSL's heartbeat feature that let attackers read memory from affected servers. It put passwords and encryption keys at risk across a large share of the web.
who invented the \"spanning tree protoco: Radia Perlman invented the Spanning Tree Protocol in 1985 while working at Digital Equipment Corporation. It prevents loops in Ethernet networks, and she is sometimes called the "Mother of the Internet".
what was the name of the security vulner: Shellshock was a major flaw in the Bash command shell, disclosed in September 2014. It let attackers run commands on affected Unix, Linux and macOS systems.
what port does http run on?: HTTP uses port 80 by default, while HTTPS uses port 443. A port number tells a computer which service a network connection is meant for.
what does the international system of qu: The International System of Quantities uses "kibibyte" (KiB) for 1,024 bytes, with the "kilobyte" (kB) meaning 1,000 bytes. The binary prefixes were created in 1998 to end the confusion.
america online (aol) started out as whic: AOL began as Quantum Link, or Q-Link, a 1985 online service for the Commodore 64. The company became America Online in 1991.
which of these is not a layer in the osi: The OSI model has seven layers: physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation and application. "Connection layer" isn't among them.
what major programming language does unr: Unreal Engine 4 is programmed mainly in C++, and it also has a visual scripting system called Blueprints. Many games on it mix the two.
what is the name of the process that sen: Quantum teleportation transfers the state of one qubit using a shared entangled pair of particles plus two classical bits of information. It doesn't move matter, and it cannot send information faster than light.
cmos is tech used for constructing integ: CMOS stands for complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor, the technology used for most modern computer chips because it uses very little power when idle. It is also the name of the small memory chip that stored BIOS settings in older PCs.
